title: Roasted Honey Soy Tofu Salad
subtitle: with Potato, Green Beans and Miso Dressing
description: Who says veggie dinners are boring? Serve up golden baked spuds, honey tofu and crunchy green beans in a moreish umami-laden miso dressing and sit down to bucketloads of flavour and texture.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 200C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil for the beans. Halve the potatoes and put in a bowl with the dashi powder, half the miso (see Did you know?) and 3 tsp vegetable oil. Combine well. Trim the beans and halve on an angle. Thinly slice the spring onion. Cut the tofu pieces into quarters.

Roast potato and tofu: Spread the potato over half the tray and roast for 15 mins or until the potato begins to colour. Add the tofu and roast for a further 10 mins or until the potato is tender and the tofu is warmed through.
Cook beans: Meanwhile, cook the beans in the pan of boiling water for 1 min or until the beans are tender and bright green. Drain and rinse under cold running water to cool.

Make salad: Combine 2 tbs mayonnaise, 1 tbs white wine vinegar, 2 tsp honey and the remaining miso in a large bowl. Add the potato, tofu, beans and half the spring onion and toss to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Divide the salad among bowls. Scatter over the sesame seeds and remaining spring onion and enjoy!

Did you know?: Miso is a thick paste made from fermented soybeans, it has a salty, rich flavour and brings lots of umami to a dish. There are three types: red, yellow and white. Generally the darker the colour, the stronger the flavour. White miso also contains fermented rice, which gives it a lighter, slightly sweet taste.
